page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Mr Lime's grapefruits
title: Mr Lime's grapefruits
description:
Mr Lime is not happy. He ordered grapefruit from Tip Top Trading, but he got pineapples. Time to say sorry! Anna has to apologise and sort everything out. How embarrassing!
This episode explores language for apologising.
phrases: I'm really sorry to hear that.
It must have been very inconvenient for you.
You have my word that we will sort this out.
And we could include some of our latest-edition imitation oranges to make up for the inconvenience.
I promise you, it won't happen again.

listening_challenge.question: How many plastic grapefruit was Mr Lime meant to receive from Tip Top Trading?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Ah hello! Welcome back to Tip Top Trading – the UK's leading wholesaler of imitation fruit. Today you're joining us in the middle of the action! Anna is with an important client Mr Lime, from Citrus Ventures. He's angry and she'll have to calm him down. She could cope brilliantly here or this could be a horrible mess!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well Mr Lime, how can I help you?

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: On Monday I was meant to receive 8,000 plastic grapefruit from Tip Top Trading.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: The delivery was made on Tuesday.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh dear.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: And instead of 8,000 plastic grapefruit, I got 800,000 plastic pineapples!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Right Anna, this is serious. You're going to have to apologise and show that you really mean it. Say: I'm really sorry to hear that.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm really sorry to hear that, Mr Lime.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: What on earth am I going to do with 800,000 plastic pineapples?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Show Mr Lime that you understand the problem. These are phrases you can use: That's totally unacceptable. That must have been very inconvenient for you. And then promise to fix the problem. Say: You have my word that we will sort this out. We can do something to make up for the inconvenience. It won't happen again.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: 800,000 plastic pineapples!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That's totally unacceptable.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: I didn't even have anywhere to put them - and pineapples are so much bigger than grapefruit!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It must have been very inconvenient for you.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: It certainly was! When he took my order, your colleague Tom told me that Tip Top Trading was the most reliable firm in the industry!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: You have my word that we will sort this out. We'll remove the pineapples and have your grapefruit sent via express delivery this afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Good. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: And we could include some of our latest-edition imitation oranges to make up for the inconvenience.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Oh! Well, that would be nice!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Tip top Anna! Excellent work and excellent words.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: They're made with revolutionary premium faux-orange, laser-curve definition technology... you will be the first to have them!

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Wow, now that's good customer service! Tell me, do you have any other artificial fruits in this range?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. Well, it's a bit of a secret, but you're a trusted client, so I think I can tell you...

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Go on...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: We're about to unveil a new Imperial Lemon.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Really?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I can't tell you any more for now. But…

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Yes...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Maybe we could present it to you more formally in a couple of weeks, when it's ready for release...?

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Sounds perfect.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: You would be the first to see it!

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Excellent. Thank you, er... Anna, isn't it?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: A very pretty name.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks. It's spelled the same forwards and backwards.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Is it really?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Anyway, Mr Lime, we'll fix this grapefruit problem for you, and I promise you, it won't happen again.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Good, good. You're new here, aren't you Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Well I look forward to working with you.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: What a success! Mr Lime has come away a very happy customer! Here are the phrases Anna used while apologising:
